listitem.para:
how many bytes can be sent/received on the inbound or outbound of a particular instance of a connection (a set of encryption/authentication keys for user packets) , from successful negotiation to expiry; acceptable values are an integer optionally followed by K, M, G, T, P or E to signify kilobytes, megabytes, gigabytes, terabytes, petabytes or exabytes.
Normally, the connection is renegotiated (via the IKE SA) before this value is reached. This option is not negotiated and both ends use their own value for this option.

The value reflects the number of bytes allowed to be encrypted with the same key. An IPsec SA uses a different key for inbound and outbound. Thus a value of 1G means that no rekey is triggered yet if the inbound has done 800M and the outboud has done 800M - while the interface has seen 1.6G of traffic.
